title: Review Open Tasks and Leave With a Clear Next Action
subtitle: Use the task list to make decisions, not to rehearse everything you owe.
description: Scan open work, remove or park stale items, clarify the next action for active commitments, and choose what deserves attention now without turning the review itself into a large planning project.

lifeOsSource.hack: Use a short task-list review to decide what is still active, what the next visible action is, and what should be parked, delegated, or removed.
lifeOsSource.whatYouDo: Scan the open list, close or park items that are no longer active, rewrite vague active work as a concrete next action, identify blocked items and their dependency, choose the small set that deserves attention now, and stop the review before it turns into doing the tasks themselves.
lifeOsSource.checkIn: What became clearer, what was removed or parked, which item is blocked, and what is the next action I can actually take?

faq.question: Do I need to review every open task every day?
faq.answer: No. Focus on the active horizon that can affect current commitments. Larger backlogs can have their own less frequent maintenance process.

faq.question: What if reviewing a task reveals a large planning problem?
faq.answer: Capture a separate planning action with the required context and return to the review. The review should clarify the work queue, not absorb every piece of work it discovers.

intro.html: A task list becomes less useful when it mixes active commitments, stale ideas, blocked work, vague projects, and items that already finished. A small review restores meaning by making a few explicit decisions and leaving each important item in a state that supports action.

sections.title: 1. Scan the active horizon
sections.html: Look at work that can affect current deadlines, commitments, dependencies, or near-term choices. Do not open the entire historical backlog unless that backlog is the object of the review.

sections.title: 2. Close, park, delegate, or clarify
sections.html: Remove completed items, park ideas that are not active, delegate work that has another owner, and rewrite vague items so the next physical or informational action is visible. Mark a dependency when no action is currently possible.

sections.title: 3. Choose the current attention set
sections.html: From the clarified list, select the small set that deserves attention based on deadlines, value, dependencies, and available capacity. Keep the remaining active work visible without promoting it all to the same priority.

sections.title: 4. Stop before review becomes execution
sections.html: If an item needs substantial planning or work, create the appropriate next action and leave it for its own block. End the review when the list is actionable enough to support the next decision; perfect organization is not the goal.

editorialCuration.reason: Replace fabricated user cohorts and retention results, unsupported time-savings, arbitrary review durations and archival thresholds, and pseudo-optimized task counts with a bounded task-list maintenance workflow.
